c1.caption: Perpendicular foot and distance.
c1.alt: Point P lies above line ell. PH is perpendicular to ell, and H is the perpendicular foot.

c1.caption: An altitude outside the triangle.
c1.alt: Triangle ABC is obtuse at B. The perpendicular from A to the line BC has foot H outside the segment BC.

c2.caption: Translation of a triangle.
c2.alt: The same horizontal translation takes A, B and C to A prime, B prime and C prime. The two triangles have equal corresponding lengths and angles.

c2.caption: Rotation through a right angle.
c2.alt: A quarter turn counterclockwise about O takes triangle ABC to triangle A prime B prime C prime.

c2.caption: Reflection across a line.
c2.alt: Reflection across the vertical line ell takes each vertex to the corresponding prime vertex and reverses the orientation of the triangle.

c3.caption: Dilation about a center.
c3.alt: A dilation about O with scale factor two takes ABC to A prime B prime C prime. Corresponding points lie on the same rays from O. In general lengths multiply by k and areas by k squared.

c4.caption: Area of a rectangle.
c4.alt: A rectangle with base b and perpendicular height h has area b times h.

c4.caption: Area with an exterior altitude.
c4.alt: The chosen base BC has length b. The perpendicular height h is AH, whose foot H lies outside BC. The area is one half b times h.

c4.caption: Equal bases and equal heights.
c4.alt: Two triangles lie between the same parallel horizontal lines. Their base lengths are both b and their heights are both h, so their areas are equal.

c4.caption: Common height and area ratio.
c4.alt: Two triangles have a common perpendicular height h. Their area ratio equals the ratio of their base lengths b one and b two.

c4.caption: Adding the areas of polygonal pieces.
c4.alt: Two diagonals divide a convex pentagon into three triangles with disjoint interiors. The area of the pentagon is the sum of the three areas.

c5.caption: A right angle.
c5.alt: Two perpendicular rays form a right angle of ninety degrees.

c5.caption: Adjacent angles on a straight line.
c5.alt: Two adjacent angles alpha and beta fill a straight angle, so their measures sum to one hundred eighty degrees.

c5.caption: Vertical angles.
c5.alt: Two intersecting lines form two equal opposite alpha angles and two equal opposite beta angles. Adjacent alpha and beta angles are not marked equal.

t1.caption: SAS congruence.
t1.alt: The corresponding sides AB and DE have one tick. AC and DF have two ticks. The included angles at A and D are equal. The correspondence is A to D, B to E, and C to F.

t1.caption: SSS congruence.
t1.alt: All three pairs of corresponding sides are marked equal using one, two, and three ticks. The correspondence is A to D, B to E, and C to F.

t1.caption: ASA congruence.
t1.alt: The angles at A and D have one arc, the angles at B and E have two arcs, and the included sides AB and DE have matching ticks. The correspondence is A to D, B to E, and C to F.

t1.caption: Two angles and a non-included side.
t1.alt: The angles at A and D have one arc, the angles at B and E have two arcs, and the non-included sides BC and EF have matching ticks. The correspondence is A to D, B to E, and C to F.

t1.caption: Hypotenuse-leg congruence.
t1.alt: Both triangles have right angles at A and D. Their hypotenuses BC and EF and legs AB and DE are marked equal. The correspondence is A to D, B to E, and C to F.

t1.caption: Equal sides and equal base angles.
t1.alt: Triangle ABC has AB equal to AC. The equal angles opposite these sides are the base angles at B and C. The equivalence also works in reverse.

t2.caption: Angles in a triangle.
t2.alt: The three interior angles alpha, beta and gamma of triangle ABC sum to one hundred eighty degrees.

t2.caption: Exterior angle of a triangle.
t2.alt: Side BC continues through C to D. The exterior angle theta at C is the sum of the remote interior angles alpha at A and beta at B.

t3.caption: Comparing opposite sides and angles.
t3.alt: In this triangle AB is longer than AC. The opposite angle gamma at C is greater than beta at B. The side and angle comparisons are equivalent.

t4.caption: Strict triangle inequality.
t4.alt: The direct side AB is shorter than the two sides AC and CB together in a nondegenerate triangle.

t4.caption: Equality for collinear points.
t4.alt: Point C lies on segment AB between A and B. Therefore the length AB equals AC plus CB.

t5.caption: Similar triangles and scale.
t5.alt: Triangles ABC and DEF have equal corresponding angles. The displayed scale factor from ABC to DEF is three halves. All lengths multiply by k and all areas by k squared.

t6.caption: Pythagoras and its converse.
t6.alt: A right triangle has legs a and b and hypotenuse c. The equation a squared plus b squared equals c squared characterizes a right angle opposite c.

p1.caption: Alternate interior angles.
p1.alt: Two parallel horizontal lines are crossed by a sloping transversal. The angle below the upper line and left of the transversal, and the angle above the lower line and right of the transversal, are both marked alpha.

p2.caption: Corresponding angles.
p2.alt: Two parallel horizontal lines are crossed by a sloping transversal. At each crossing the angle above the parallel line and right of the transversal is marked alpha.

p2.caption: Same-side interior angles.
p2.alt: Two parallel horizontal lines are crossed by a sloping transversal. The two interior angles on the right of the transversal are marked alpha and beta, with alpha plus beta equal to 180 degrees.

o1.caption: A radius perpendicular to a tangent.
o1.alt: A circle with center O meets a vertical tangent line at T. The radius OT and the tangent form a marked right angle.

o2.caption: Equal tangent segments from an exterior point.
o2.alt: The two segments PA and PB touch a circle at A and B. Matching marks show that PA and PB have equal lengths. Dashed radii OA and OB each meet the corresponding tangent at a marked right angle.

o2.caption: On the circle: one tangent. Inside: no tangents; the drawn lines are secants.
o2.alt: Left: P lies on the circle and has one tangent. Right: P lies inside the circle. Each of the two drawn lines through P crosses the circle at two marked points, so both lines are secants; no tangent passes through P.
